title: Data labeling edgecases scratchpad (Asha)
content:
Quick scratchpad for label cleanup + edge-cases. Mostly notes to self and examples to bring to sync with Ryan.

Context:
- Running final cleanup pass on conversational intent/response labeling dataset for routing model. Found ~1.2k ambiguous samples flagged by validator. Need consistent rules for: partial answers, multi-intent, system instruction echoes, and profanity masking.
- Goal: reduce inter-annotator disagreement to <6% on held out batch.

High-level rules (draft):
1) Primary intent labeling: pick the user intent that best explains the user's explicit ask. If user asks 2 distinct asks in one message (e.g., "Reset my password and delete account"), label as MULTI_INTENT.
2) Partial answers from assistant: when the assistant answers incompletely (e.g., starts to answer then stops), label assistant_response_quality = PARTIAL. If user follows up to clarify, mark original as INCOMPLETE_CONSUMER.
3) System instructions present: if message contains an explicit system instruction echo (e.g., "As an AI assistant, I cannot..."), strip the leading instruction for intent detection. Only label the remainder. Mark tag SYSTEM_ECHO.
4) Profanity / PII masking: do not change label intent because of profanity. Add tag SENSITIVE if >1 token of PII (email, ssn, phone) or profanity retained. If PII is masked (***), treat as non-sensitive.
5) Reroutes and clarifying questions: when assistant asks for clarification before taking action, label intent as CLARIFICATION_REQUEST if it expects disambiguation. If follow-up is clearly an action request, keep original intent.

Examples (ambiguous ones flagged):
- "Can you schedule a meeting next Thursday? Also, what's the wifi password?"
  -> label: MULTI_INTENT ; tags: [SCHEDULING, INFO_REQUEST]

- "I think my account is hacked. I changed my password yesterday but still locked out. What do I do?"
  -> label: ACCOUNT_RECOVERY ; tag: URGENT (if words like locked out / hacked)

- "As an AI, I can't browse the web, but here's how you'd do it: ..." (assistant message)
  -> intent: NA (system assistant_message) ; tag: SYSTEM_ECHO

- "Uh, sure?" (short ambiguous user reply after assistant asked clarifying Q)
  -> label: CLARIFICATION_YES (treat as confirmation if context shows it responds to question). If insufficient context, label NEEDS_CONTEXT.

Open edge-cases we've seen (notes):
- Multi-intent but one sub-intent is rhetorical. E.g., "Does this app track me? Also, what's the refund policy?" If first is rhetorical (no action asked), classify as SINGLE_INTENT (REFUND) unless user clearly seeks answer to first. Need heuristics: if sentence contains a question mark + explicit ask words (how, what, where) treat as ask.
- Quoted content that contains an intent inside quotes (user pastes email: "He said: 'Please cancel my subscription'"). Should label based on user's meta-intent (why they pasted). Add rule: If user pastes secondary content without explicit ask, treat as INFORMATION_SHARING not ACTION.
- Long system logs pasted: mostly noise. If >30% tokens look like log-like (timestamps, stack traces), label as TECH_SUPPORT_LOG and mark as NO_INTENT for routing (send to human triage).

Annotation heuristics (for the cleanup pass):
- When in doubt, add COMMENT tag and mark sample for review rather than flipping label. We can later batch-review COMMENTed samples with 2+ reviewers.
- Use conservative labeling: prefer NEEDS_CONTEXT over guessing.

TODOs / action items for next sync w/ Ryan (priority order):
- [ ] Export current validator disagreement set (JIRA-7892) and split by rule type (partial answers, multi-intent, system echo, pasted content).
- [ ] Write automated heuristic to detect quoted content vs direct ask (start simple: regex for quote chars + short length).
- [ ] Add unit tests for profanity/PII tag logic in labeling scripts repo. PR reference above.
- [ ] Prepare ~200 gold examples for retraining (balanced across edge-cases). I can draft 50 this week.
- [ ] Clarify with product: desired behavior for rhetorical vs actionable questions. Ping @product in Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-1248).

Questions for review meeting:
- What threshold for log-like content to route to human triage? (30% ? 50%?)
- Do we want to keep SYSTEM_ECHO as a downstream tag or strip it before model training? My vote: keep as tag but strip content during training.
- How to treat multi-intent prioritization in single-label training vs multi-label routing? (We currently have routing that supports MULTI_INTENT flag).

Notes to self (formatting / data work):
- When running cleanup script, output CSV with columns: id, orig_label, new_label, reason_tag, reviewer. Keep small freeform reason to trace.
- Quick heuristic rules drafted in /scripts/labeling heuristics/simple_rules.py (see PR).

Example sample bank (for later copy/paste into gold set):
1) "Please cancel my subscription. Also, how do I change my billing address?" -> MULTI_INTENT
2) "My card failed, but the app still charged me" -> BILLING_ISSUE ; tag: CHARGED_AFTER_FAILURE
3) "I keep getting an error: 502 at /api/login, stack: ..." -> TECH_SUPPORT_LOG ; tag: LOG_PRESENT
4) User message: "Thanks! :)" (following a confirmation) -> GRATITUDE_CONFIRM ; treat as NO_ACTION

Rough disagreement examples I will attach to JIRA: (short excerpts)
- Sample 3421: annotator A labeled REFUND, B labeled MULTI_INTENT. Raw: "Do I get a refund if I return it? Also, is shipping covered?" -> likely MULTI_INTENT but need product input.
- Sample 3987: annotator labels CHITCHAT vs CUSTOMER_FEEDBACK. Raw: "I love the colors, btw" -> CHITCHAT (unless in product review flow).

Endnotes:
- This doc is messy; will formalize into a Confluence page after sync. For now, keep as scratchpad.
- If time, write a tiny validation job to auto-tag SYSTEM_ECHO and TECH_SUPPORT_LOG before human annotation to lower disagreement.

-- Asha
